presidentialSuccession.name: Ollanta Humala
presidentialSuccession.notes: The Partido Nacionalista del Perú is listed among FSP active members in Regalado's 2007 roster (Encuentros y desencuentros, Ocean Sur 2008).

presidentialSuccession.name: Pedro Castillo
presidentialSuccession.notes: Perú Libre joined the FSP in 2018–2020, before Castillo's 2021 win on its ticket. Removed and arrested after his December 2022 attempt to dissolve Congress.

presidentialSuccession.name: José Jerí
presidentialSuccession.notes: Assumed the presidency as head of Congress after Boluarte's removal; censured and removed 17 February 2026 amid the "Chifa-gate" scandal.

presidentialSuccession.name: José María Balcázar
presidentialSuccession.notes: Elected interim president by Congress 18–19 Feb 2026 on Perú Libre's nomination (he entered Congress on its ticket, though formally unaffiliated after caucus moves). Interim only: Keiko Fujimori (Fuerza Popular), winner of the June 2026 runoff, is due to be sworn in on 28 July 2026.

fspParties.note: Peru has two documented FSP members. The Partido Nacionalista Peruano (Ollanta Humala) appears on Regalado's 2008 roster and led the Gana Perú alliance to power in 2011. Perú Libre (Vladimir Cerrón) joined the Forum as Perú Libertario at the XXIV Encuentro (Havana 2018) and announced its formal incorporation as a full member on 30 June 2020; the Forum publicly defended Cerrón against what it called political persecution in 2021. Perú Libre won the 2021 election with Pedro Castillo and, after the interim churn of 2025–26, provided the congressionally elected interim president José María Balcázar (Feb 2026).

legislativeControl.seats: The PNP (founded 2005) had no presence before 2011; Congress was dominated by Fujimorismo, APRA and Perú Posible.
Gana Perú won 47 of 130 seats — the largest bloc but short of a majority; Humala governed with a working majority assembled with Perú Posible.
The PNP won no seats in 2016 and left Congress; Perú Libre (an FSP member from 2018–2020) had not yet entered Congress.
Perú Libre won 37 of 130 seats — the largest bloc but far short of a majority; Castillo governed through a permanent governability crisis and the caucus fragmented.
Under Boluarte and the interim presidencies Perú Libre sat in opposition with a diminished caucus; in February 2026 Congress elected its lawmaker José María Balcázar interim president.

government.note: Gana Perú was the largest bloc (47/130) but well short of a 66-seat majority. Humala assembled a working majority with Alejandro Toledo's Perú Posible (21 seats); that partnership was fragile and the government's congressional support fluctuated over the term.

Perú Libre was the largest bloc (37/130) but even with its left ally Juntos por el Perú held barely a third of the chamber. Castillo faced two impeachment attempts before Congress removed him in December 2022 after he tried to dissolve it; his own caucus fragmented along the way.
